::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Status:** starter entry, open for contributions. Not a LENS consensus.
:::

## Core question

Does the model structure itself prevent the parameter from being determined, even with perfect,
noise-free, unlimited data? Collecting more of the same data cannot fix structural
non-identifiability. Only changing the model, the observations, or the information supplied
(constraints, priors, external data) can.

## Definitions across fields

### Systems biology and dynamical systems

> A parameter is structurally non-identifiable when it cannot be determined uniquely even from
> ideal, noise-free model output. This typically happens because of a functional relationship
> among parameters (a manifold of parameter values that produce the same output).
> [@bellman1970structural; @raue2009structural]

In profile-likelihood terms, the profile likelihood of a structurally non-identifiable
parameter is **flat**. [@raue2009structural]

### Statistical ecology (parameter redundancy)

> A model is parameter-redundant if it can be rewritten in terms of fewer parameters. A
> parameter-redundant model is not identifiable. [@catchpole1997detecting; @cole2020parameter]

Parameter redundancy is checked symbolically, through the rank of a derivative matrix of an
exhaustive summary of the model. This gives the number of estimable combinations, and which
ones they are.

### Statistics

> The model $\{P_\theta\}$ fails to be identifiable: distinct $\theta$ give the same $P_\theta$.
> See [identifiability](identifiability.qmd). [@rothenberg1971identification]

## Formal statement

There exist $\theta_1 \neq \theta_2$ with $P_{\theta_1} = P_{\theta_2}$. Typically the set
$\{\theta : P_\theta = P_{\theta_0}\}$ is a manifold of positive dimension. Its dimension is the
number of parameters minus the number of estimable combinations, i.e. the deficiency in
@catchpole1997detecting.

## Examples

- $Y \sim N(a + b, 1)$: only $a + b$ is estimable; the deficiency is 1.
- Grouped or normalised likelihoods: if a likelihood depends on predictors only through
  within-group shares (e.g. a multinomial allocation within each group), any term that is
  constant within a group cancels and is structurally non-identifiable. An external anchor that
  varies within groups is needed to identify it.
- Capture–recapture models where survival and capture probability for the final occasion
  appear only as a product. [@catchpole1997detecting]

## Connections and distinctions

- **vs. [practical identifiability](practical-identifiability.qmd):** structural problems come
  from the model and persist with infinite data; practical problems come from limited, noisy
  data.
- **[Partial identification](partial-identification.qmd):** the non-identified direction may
  still be bounded, giving an identified set rather than a point.
- **[Recoverability](recoverability.qmd):** *(proposed)* the estimable combinations are
  exactly the functionals that remain recoverable.

## Key references

- @bellman1970structural: origin of "structural identifiability".
- @raue2009structural: the profile likelihood distinguishes structural from practical problems.
- @catchpole1997detecting and @cole2020parameter: parameter redundancy and symbolic detection.

## Open questions

- *(open)* Symbolic rank methods scale poorly. What is the right check for high-dimensional
  hierarchical or spatial models with thousands of latent effects?
